title: The Message From the Other Island

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A paddler warns that raiders are gathering against the village: trust the warning, or suspect a trick.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A lone paddler from a neighboring island has arrived, exhausted, with a warning: the raiders are gathering canoes, and the village is their target. (subject) believes (other.him/her) completely. (friend) points out that nobody knows this paddler, and that the warning might be meant to draw the warriors away from the village. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village prepares: the children to the caves, the stores hidden, the warriors on the beach. The raiders come three nights later, see the village ready and waiting, and turn back without landing. The paddler is given a feast and a canoe full of food.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) keeps the warriors at home and sends scouts instead. The scouts come back with nothing. The raiders never come. Whether the warning was false, or whether the raiders saw the scouts and gave up, nobody ever learns. The paddler leaves quietly.
